draft.overall: Among the counted names, 6 ran at least 50 percent above the prior close, and 5 of them kept at least half of the peak gain at the close; none of them gave the entire move back. The two covered 50 percent movers with the highest peaks were AMOD, with fresh news found in our sources: Alpha Modus reported completion of a shares-for-Bitcoin PIPE, and CYCU, with fresh news found in our sources: Cycurion disclosed that Nasdaq confirmed it had regained compliance with the $1.00 minimum-bid requirement. After the close, MI added 14 percent. 6 of the 12 names the desk covers had fresh news in our sources.

lines.text: The catalyst is not fresh: on September 30, VCIG disclosed an equity purchase agreement giving it the right to direct Hudson Global Ventures to purchase up to $125 million of ordinary shares, alongside registration of up to 100,000,000 ELOC purchase shares and related shares. The financing creates substantial potential share supply, subject to transaction conditions, registration, conversion, and exercise requirements.

The catalyst is not fresh: on August 17, ZNB completed a $10.0 million private placement of 3,412,970 units at $2.93 per unit, each containing an ordinary share and a warrant exercisable at $4.40. The financing added shares and immediately exercisable warrants, leaving issued shares and broader financing capacity as structural risks.

On October 1, Silo agreed to acquire software, technology, and related intellectual property from Norsight Consulting for warrants covering up to 300,000 common shares at a $1.51 exercise price, exercisable for five years. The transaction adds those assets while creating warrant supply, and stockholder-approval limitations prevent the presently eligible amount from being fully established from the excerpt.

Alpha Modus reported completion of a shares-for-Bitcoin PIPE in which its subsidiary received 3,170 Bitcoin valued above $250 million; secondary coverage reported 51.6 million common shares and matching warrants. The balance-sheet change is paired with substantial dilution and supply considerations.

The catalyst is not fresh: on September 18, SmartKem filed an S-1 covering prospective resale of up to 30,000,000 shares and an S-3 registering resale of up to 15,127,662 shares, including 2,516,786 additional conversion shares. The filings describe substantial prospective resale capacity, with supply and dilution overhang dependent on effectiveness and issuance or resale.

On October 2, Cycurion disclosed that Nasdaq confirmed it had regained compliance with the $1.00 minimum-bid requirement after its August 28, 2026 1-for-8 reverse split and 10 consecutive trading days above $1.00. The disclosure removed the immediate minimum-bid-price deficiency, while the reported 48% reaction made it an identifiable session catalyst.
Research was not completed at this checkpoint, and no dossier is on file.

The catalyst is not fresh: on September 28, the effective 1-for-15 reverse stock split consolidated every 15 outstanding common shares into one share and changed the CUSIP. It was a mechanical capital-structure action, not a new operating, clinical, commercial, or financing catalyst.

SMX published three October 2 company releases about its Digital Material Passport and certified recycled plastic positioning. The updates concerned its material-verification platform, but the supplied evidence identifies no contract, customer commitment, approval, revenue contribution, or other quantified commercial result.

On October 1, QTREX reported that an independent test of its cryogenic interconnect at 20 mK found more than 100 dB of channel isolation across the 4 to 8 GHz qubit band, stated as 60 dB beyond the market leader. The result is a quantified product-performance claim linked to a prospective commercial agreement that had not yet been executed or disclosed.
Research was not completed at this checkpoint, and no dossier is on file.

On September 30, NFT Ltd disclosed an agreement to sell 80,000,000 Class A ordinary shares to non-U.S. purchasers at $0.45 per share for approximately $36 million, subject to closing conditions. The proposed placement is substantial prospective share supply and materially dilutive if it closes, but the bundle does not confirm completion or issuance.
